named.name: Shittim
named.label: right
named.note: Israel set out from here and camped by the Jordan three days (3:1-2).

named.name: Adam
named.label: right
named.note: The waters stood up in a heap "a great way off, at Adam, the city beside Zarethan" (3:16), usually placed at Tell ed-Damiyeh, about 30 km upstream.

named.name: Zarethan
named.label: right
named.note: Named with Adam in 3:16; often placed at Tell es-Sa’idiyeh.

named.name: Gilgal
named.label: below
named.note: First camp west of the Jordan, "on the eastern border of Jericho" (4:19). Its exact site is uncertain.

moves.text: The people cross on dry ground opposite Jericho
The waters stop and stand in a heap far upstream

symbols.key: Twelve stones in the Jordan and at Gilgal
Twelve stones in the Jordan and at Gilgal

p: The text places the stopping of the waters at Adam, far upstream, and the crossing "opposite Jericho" (3:16). The Jordan was in flood at harvest time (3:15). Earthquakes have blocked the river near Damiyeh in recorded history, most famously in 1927; the text presents the event as the work of the Lord at the moment the priests stepped in.
About the routes. Places are located from OpenBible.info. The lines between them are reconstructions drawn for teaching, not paths the text describes.
